generatedProse.concept-context: In any subject, research ethics is part of how sound work is defined, not a hurdle cleared before the work begins. Recognised principles run across disciplines: participants are respected, consent is informed, harm is minimised, and methods and findings are reported honestly. A project that treats its ethics application as paperwork, rather than a design discipline, is weak however polished its write-up looks.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students preparing the same study for ethical approval.

{{learner-a}} treats the ethics application as a form to clear. The consent wording says nothing about how data will be stored, participation is described as expected of the group being recruited, and a relevant personal connection goes undeclared. The study may still gain approval, but it sits uneasily against the principles of informed participation, transparency and declared interest.

{{learner-b}} reads the same design against each principle in turn. Participation is made genuinely voluntary and informed, storage and responsibility are spelled out, and any connection is declared openly. Nothing about the study is hidden, so the application documents a design that is sound rather than merely permitted.

Both students submit a form. Only {{learner-b}} used the principles to improve the research itself, which is what treating ethics as integrity rather than paperwork means.
generatedProse.summary: Research ethics is the substance behind the ethics form, not the form itself. You can now justify ethical conduct as an expression of academic integrity, evaluate a research design against the six recognised principles of ethical research, and anticipate the issues an ethics application must address. The next lesson turns to the duties you take on once you start collecting data from participants.

check.body: A study plans to recruit participants by telling them their tutor expects them to take part. Which principle of ethical research does this most clearly breach?

items.text: That participation should, wherever possible, be voluntary and appropriately informed.
That research should maximise benefit and minimise harm.
That lines of responsibility should be clearly defined.
That the independence of research should be maintained.

feedback.correct: That's right. Telling participants that a tutor expects them to take part makes participation no longer freely voluntary.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Which principle is about the freedom to take part?
feedback.incorrectFinal: Recruiting through a tutor's expectation breaches voluntary, informed participation; the other principles concern outcomes, accountability and independence.

_prompts.concept-context: What does this look like in practice within the given context? Write a short follow-on from the generic definition above, in the learner's own subject or discipline. Keep it to two or three sentences, mid-register, following straight on from the generic definition.
_prompts.worked-example: Give a subject-specific worked example of this lesson's concept: a weaker or less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice, using the context cast (character tokens) consistently. Keep the weaker-then-stronger shape and the two-part contrast; carry the cast only through the {{learner-a}} (weaker) and {{learner-b}} (stronger) tokens, never a literal name (the pack supplies the whole body, but not the names). Each example paragraph must begin with its token, weaker first - merge-context.js's wrapProse() only emits the we-weaker/we-stronger cue classes for a paragraph that leads with the token. The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
_prompts.summary: Recap what the learner can now do, in terms of their own subject or context. One short paragraph. Do not restate the learning outcomes verbatim.
_prompts.check: Write the subject's own version of this lesson's check question(s), testing the same outcome in the learner's own discipline. Keep the same number of items and the same correctness pattern as the generic version; reword the stem and items for the subject. Keep the component-level feedback (correct / notFinal / final) teaching, never a bare verdict.
